gaps.quote: By the endpoint contract the physical output is
gaps.note: The condition called the endpoint contract is never stated on the page (the paper's condition M_out(rho(w)) - M_in(w) = I_m, line 1467, plus s<Wm), nor the composition rule Phi_{M'}Phi_M = Phi_{M'+M} (paper line 1508), so the reader cannot check that the product of frames equals Phi_{I_m}.

gaps.quote: Each stream has volume $V/W$ and row count divisible by $W^{k-1}$
gaps.note: The page never introduces a row field preceding both chunks, nor the hypothesis that its length is divisible by W^k (paper lines 1482-1484, 1502). Without it the cyclic split and the divisibility by W^{k-1} do not follow; the reader cannot tell what rows are.

gaps.quote: Joining them, the high parts form a row field of range $R=q^{2\rho}\ge W^{k'}$ before both remaining chunks.
gaps.note: The page never gives the field-order construction (paper lines 1660-1676): split each chunk into top rho digits and rest, exchange the high digits, move h+ next to d+. Nor does it say that padded rows are scanned away and the joining moves reversed at the end (lines 1708-1713), nor that this movement costs O(V rho) = O(V log(2e)), absorbed into O(V e^tau). The reader cannot see how the pieces give the full interchange or why the total is O(V e^tau).

This needs 1 <= rho < e, which the paper (line 1656) only gets for sufficiently large e, handling the bounded set of small widths by individual digit interchanges (line 1657). The page states it for every e, where e-rho could be negative.
